transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I've been struggling a lot lately with listening when people talk to me. Even when someone is speaking directly to me, my mind just drifts off and I miss what they're saying. It's starting to cause some real problems in my daily life.
Do you also find yourself frequently fidgeting, feeling restless, or having trouble sitting still, especially in quiet environments?
No, I don't really experience those physical symptoms. I don't have trouble sitting still or feel restless like that. It's more that my mind wanders, rather than my body being active.
When did you first start noticing these difficulties with paying attention and your mind wandering, was it in childhood or did it start more recently?
I actually first noticed these difficulties back in childhood, definitely before I turned 12. However, they have become a consistent, daily struggle for about the past two years.
Can you tell me more about how these difficulties with paying attention have affected your daily life, such as your work, relationships, or hobbies, over the past two years?

Over the past two years, I've had a really hard time organizing my tasks and activities, which makes keeping up with my work a constant struggle. Also, because I often fail to listen when people are speaking directly to me, it has caused a lot of tension and misunderstandings in my personal relationships.
Are you easily distracted by your surroundings, such as noise or movement, or is it more that you have trouble sustaining focus on tasks and activities even when the environment is quiet and calm?

I'm not completely sure, and I haven't really thought about it in that way before. My main difficulties are just that I have a really hard time organizing my tasks and I often don't listen well when people are speaking directly to me.
Can you think of any situations where you are able to focus and pay attention without difficulty, such as during hobbies or activities that you find particularly interesting?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed any specific hobbies or activities where I can focus without difficulty. I generally find it hard to stay focused on almost anything I try to do.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking, blurt out answers before questions have been completed, or have difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations or activities?

No, I don't really have those issues at all. I don't interrupt people or blurt things out, and I'm fine with waiting my turn. My struggles are much more about zoning out rather than acting impulsively.
Are there any other symptoms or difficulties you're experiencing that you haven't mentioned yet, which might help me better understand your situation?

No, I don't think there is anything else. Those two main issues—not being able to listen properly when spoken to and struggling to organize my daily tasks—are really the core of what I'm dealing with.
This conversation is now concluded. The patient's symptoms align with the diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation).

Thank you, Doctor. That diagnosis makes a lot of sense given how long I've struggled with listening to others and keeping my tasks organized. I really appreciate you helping me understand what is going on.
